questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

The farmer walked beside his bulls, isn’t it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "didn't he"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate substitution for the given statement is "didn't he".
 
• As here the subject is a farmer, who is a living thing and we can not use the word "it" for this situation.
 
• As per the rules of grammar if the first sentence is in the past form then the following question tag should also be in past form, so it should be "didn't" instead of "isn't".
 
 
• *Example: She ate a pie, didn't she?*​
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the above explanation the most accurate substitution is "didn't he".​

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information​__** Let us see why the other options are not correct. 

 
• option 2 **"****did he"** is incorrect because the question statement is in negative form but it will convert it into a positive form.
 
• option 4 **"didn't they"** is incorrect because the word "**they"** is used for plural but here we are talking about farmer which is singular.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The children were / bubbling with excitement / at the thought of / seeing sea.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**seeing sea**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**seeing sea**" is **missing an article**.
 
• An **article** gives **information** about the** noun** by coming** in front** of it.
 
• As the sentence **denotes** a **specific sea**, the article "**the**" must be used. 
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase will be "**seeing the sea**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Articles** are divided into **definite and indefinite articles.**
 
• "**The**" is the **definite article** as it denotes the **particular noun**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Let us eat from **the shop** near our school.* 
 
 
 
• **"A"** and **"an"** are** indefinite articles** as they denote **any noun. **
 
• **"A"** is used before a noun that does **not begin with a vowel sound**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Mike is **a teacher. ***
 
 
 
• **"An"** is used before a noun **beginning with a vowel sound.** 
 
 
• **Example: ***Elly saw **an elephant** yesterday. *

• *Example: I am having **confusion** about this chapter.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Please don’t confuse me __by giving so man__y different directions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**no substitution required**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**By giving so many**" is grammatically **correct**.
 
• The **preposition** **"by"** is used to show **how work is done**.
 
 
• **Example:*** Mike travels **by** bus. *
 
 
 
• The **verb "giving**" is in the correct form of a tense, which is **present continuous** because the action is going on. 
 
 
• **Example:** *Sera is **giving** massages at a nearby parlour.* 
 
 
 
• The **phrase "so many"** denotes the **unspecific quantity**. 
 
 
• **Example:** *Martha has **so many** works left undone. *
 
 
 
• As the phrase "by giving so many" justifies its usage, no substitution is required. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **sentence** must justify the **subject-verb concord** to be grammatically correct. 
 
• **The subject** is the **noun or pronoun** about which the sentence is. 
 
• Subject-verb concord means the **subject and verb must agree in number.**
 
• If the **subject is singular**, the **verb** should also be **singular** and if the **subject** is **plural**, the **verb** must also be **plural**. 
 
 
• **Example:** *The **boys want** to play cricket but **she wants** to play basketball. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In English grammar, certain verbs are followed directly by an object (if there is one) without a preposition; such verbs are known as “**preposition-less verbs.”** 
 
• In this case,** 'reach'** is one such verb that doesn't need a preposition ('to') after it when indicating a destination.
 
• As a general rule, the correct usage should be** 'reach + (place)' **— e.g., 'reach Delhi', 'reach the station' — and not '**reach to (place)**'.
 
• Therefore, the phrase** "reached to Delhi"** is incorrect. The correct phrasing should be** "reached Delhi."**

Therefore, the **correct answer** is - **"reached to Delhi."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is correct as it stands. "we will have" is part of a future perfect construction, which is a tense used to describe an action that will be completed before some specified point in the future.
 
• **Option 3 **is also correct. "By this time tomorrow" is a common way to reference a specific time in the future.
 
• **Option 2**, 'No error', is incorrect since there is an error in the sentence.

The correct option is** "corrective".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• It means to make something right that is wrong. 

 
 
• ** Example-*** She had corrective surgery on her knee.*
 
• ***Remedial*** means aimed at improving or correcting.
 
 
 
• ***Example-** The government took remedial actions to repair the bridge*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Superficial **means not thinking or doing something in a complete way.

 
 
• **Example -*** She has a superficial knowledge of her subject.*
 
 
 
• **Harmfu**l means causing harm.
 
 
• **Example **- *Fumes produced after burning plastic are harmful to human health.*
 
 
 
• **Medicinal** - useful for curing illness.
 
 
• ** Example:** *Medicinal plants are used to treat cancer.*
